lessons.title: The OFFICIAL Shopify Tutorial For Beginners (Part 1)
objectives: Describe what a hosted store platform gives you and what it costs
Judge whether a full store is the right first step for a given seller
Set up the basics of a store without paying for things you do not need
lessons.notes:
Shopify is a hosted shop: you pay monthly and get a website that takes orders, manages stock and handles payment, without building anything. It is the industry standard and the tutorial is worth following. It is also not where most Kenyan sellers should start, and it is worth being clear about that before anyone commits.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY GIVES YOU: a professional storefront on your own name, stock that decrements itself, order management, and the ability to grow without rebuilding. Real advantages once you have volume.

WHAT IT COSTS: a monthly fee in foreign currency, a domain, usually a theme or an app or two, plus payment processing. That is a fixed bill arriving every month whether or not you sell anything, and for a seller doing a handful of orders a week it can exceed the profit.

THE HONEST SEQUENCE for most sellers here: start where the customers already are and where setup costs nothing — WhatsApp Business, Instagram, Facebook, or a marketplace. Prove that people buy the product. Build the customer list. Then, when order volume makes the monthly cost trivial and the manual work is eating your day, move to a hosted store. Selling nothing on a professional site is worse than selling steadily through WhatsApp.

IF YOU DO SET ONE UP, the essentials: one clear product page per item with real photographs, a delivery policy stated plainly, a returns policy, contact details a person can actually reach, and payment methods your customers use.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — the friction that decides whether a Kenyan store converts. PAYMENT: card checkout is unfamiliar to many buyers, so offer M-Pesa and pay-on-delivery where you can, because the store that only takes cards will lose most of its traffic at the last step. TRUST: buyers here have good reason to be cautious about paying a stranger online, so a physical address, a real phone number answered by a person, and visible customer photographs do more for conversion than any theme. And SPEED: most visitors are on a phone on mobile data, so compress every image and test the page on a bundle rather than on wifi.
lessons.practice: Work out the real monthly cost of running a hosted store - subscription, domain, any apps, payment fees - and the profit per sale on one real product. Divide to find how many orders a month it takes before the store pays for itself. Then decide honestly whether to start there or on a free channel, and write your reason in one sentence.

quiz.question: When does a hosted store become the right choice?
options: When order volume makes the monthly cost trivial and manual work is eating the day
As soon as someone decides to sell online
Once the product photographs are ready
When a domain name is available

quiz.question: What most often loses a Kenyan store its sale at the last step?
options: Offering only card checkout, when buyers expect M-Pesa or pay on delivery

lessons.title: 4 simple steps to become a Jumia seller
objectives: Decide whether a marketplace suits what you sell
Understand what the marketplace takes and what it gives
Prepare a listing that can actually win in a crowded category
lessons.notes:
A marketplace brings you buyers who are already there and already intending to purchase. That is the whole value, and it is substantial: you are not solving the hardest problem in online selling, which is getting anyone to visit at all.

WHAT YOU GIVE UP in exchange: a commission on each sale, their rules on pricing, returns and delivery, and — most importantly — the customer relationship. The buyer belongs to the marketplace, not to you. They can change terms, and a competitor can appear beside your listing at a lower price.

WHAT SELLS WELL THERE: things people search for by name and compare on price and delivery — electronics, accessories, household goods, anything standard. What sells badly: anything that needs explaining, anything where the maker is the reason to buy, anything handmade or unusual, because the format flattens everything into a price comparison.

WINNING IN A CROWDED CATEGORY comes down to the things sellers neglect: a title that contains the words people actually search including brand, model and size; real photographs on a clean background rather than the supplier's stock image everyone else is also using; a description that answers the questions asked in the comments; accurate stock so you never cancel an order; and fast dispatch, because delivery speed is ranked and is what buyers compare.

DO THE ARITHMETIC BEFORE LISTING. Commission, any fees, packaging, the cost of returns and the time spent. A product that looks profitable at the shop counter can lose money on a marketplace once the commission and a return are counted.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — the strategy that actually works here is to use BOTH. The marketplace is where strangers find you; your own WhatsApp or social channel is where repeat customers come back without commission. So put something in the parcel — a card with your number and a reason to message you directly next time — and treat the first sale as paid customer acquisition. Also be realistic about the working capital: money from marketplace sales arrives on a settlement cycle, not immediately, so you need enough cash to buy the next stock before you are paid for the last, and that gap is what breaks small sellers.
lessons.practice: Choose one real product and do the full arithmetic for selling it on a marketplace: cost, commission, packaging, delivery, an allowance for returns, and what is left. Then look at the three listings currently ranking for it and write down exactly what they have that you would need - title wording, photographs, stock, dispatch speed.

quiz.question: What do you give up on a marketplace?
options: The customer relationship - the buyer belongs to the marketplace, not to you
The ability to photograph your own products

quiz.question: What breaks small marketplace sellers financially?
options: The settlement gap - needing cash for new stock before being paid for the last

lessons.title: The OFFICIAL Shopify Tutorial For Beginners 2026 (Part 2)
objectives: Build product pages that answer a buyer's questions before they ask
Set up delivery and payment so the checkout does not lose people
Test the whole buying journey as a customer before launching
lessons.notes:
Part 1 was the shop. This is the part where sales are won or lost: the product page and the checkout.

A PRODUCT PAGE HAS TO ANSWER EVERYTHING a buyer would ask in a shop. What exactly is it, size and measurements, what is included, condition, how long delivery takes, what it costs to deliver to them, what happens if it is wrong. Every unanswered question is a reason to leave, and online they simply leave rather than asking.

PHOTOGRAPHS DO MOST OF THE SELLING, which Module 3 covers properly. Several angles, the thing in use, something for scale.

SET DELIVERY UP HONESTLY. A price that looks good and then adds a large delivery charge at the last step is the most common reason a cart is abandoned anywhere. Show delivery cost early, or build it into the price and say delivery is included — buyers strongly prefer the second.

PAYMENT: offer what people actually use. For most Kenyan buyers that means M-Pesa, and pay on delivery for anyone not ready to send money to a shop they do not know. Every payment method you do not offer is a share of buyers you do not get.

THEN BUY FROM YOUR OWN SHOP. Complete a real order, on a phone, on mobile data, with a payment method you actually offer. Beginners launch without ever testing the checkout and discover the fault from a customer who is now annoyed — if they bother to tell you at all.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — write the POLICIES before launch, in plain language, and put them where they can be found: how long delivery takes to different areas, what delivery costs, what happens if an item is damaged or wrong, and whether you take returns. In a market where buyers are rightly cautious about online sellers, a clear returns policy is not a liability, it is a selling point. And name the delivery method — courier, boda, parcel service, collection point — because 'we deliver countrywide' means nothing to someone deciding whether to trust you with money.
lessons.practice: Build one complete product page answering every question a buyer would ask, then write your delivery and returns policies in plain language. Finally, place a real order on your own store from a phone on mobile data, pay with a method you actually offer, and note every point where you hesitated or something confused you.

quiz.question: What is the most common reason a cart is abandoned?
options: A delivery charge appearing late, after the price looked good

quiz.question: Why is a clear returns policy a selling point here?
options: Buyers are rightly cautious about online sellers, so it reduces the risk they feel
It reduces the number of returns

lessons.title: How to Sell Products on WhatsApp | Full Tutorial
objectives: Run a genuine selling operation on WhatsApp Business
Handle enquiries so they turn into orders rather than fading out
Keep records when there is no shop system doing it for you
lessons.notes:
For a great many Kenyan sellers this is not a stepping stone to a real shop. It IS the shop, and it outsells the website. Treat it as the main channel it is.

SET UP WHATSAPP BUSINESS PROPERLY, because it is free and most sellers use a fraction of it: the CATALOGUE, so you can send a product instead of describing it; QUICK REPLIES for the questions you answer forty times a week — price, delivery, location, payment; a GREETING and AWAY MESSAGE so nobody is met with silence at 10pm; LABELS to mark which conversations are new enquiries, awaiting payment, or to be delivered; and a complete profile with location and hours.

REPLY FAST. This is the whole game. A buyer messaging three sellers buys from whoever answers first with a clear price. Slow replies do not lose you politeness points, they lose you the order to the next person.

ANSWER THE FULL QUESTION AT ONCE. Price, whether it is in stock, delivery cost to them, how to pay, how long it takes. Making a buyer extract each fact one message at a time is how enquiries die.

STATUS IS YOUR SHOP WINDOW. People who saved your number see it daily. New stock, a customer's order going out, a price list once a week. This reaches exactly the people most likely to buy again and costs nothing.

KEEP RECORDS, because nothing here does it for you. A simple sheet: date, customer, item, price, delivery cost, paid or not, delivered or not. Without it you will lose an order, forget a debt, and have no idea at month end whether you made money.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — three things that protect you. Confirm every order back in writing — item, price, delivery cost, address, total — so there is no argument later about what was agreed. Decide your PAYMENT RULE and state it the same way every time: paid in advance, deposit, or on delivery. Pay on delivery wins more sales and costs you the occasional wasted trip, so price that in rather than pretending it does not happen. And keep customer numbers and details as what they are — other people's personal information — used for their orders, not sold or added to lists they never asked to join.
lessons.practice: Set up WhatsApp Business fully: catalogue with real photographs and prices, five quick replies for your most common questions, greeting and away messages, and labels. Then write your standard order confirmation message and your payment rule. Start the record sheet today, even with one order, and post one price list to Status this week.

quiz.question: What decides who gets the order when a buyer messages three sellers?
options: Whoever answers first with a clear, complete price
Whoever has been in business longest

quiz.question: Why confirm every order back in writing?
options: It removes any later argument about item, price, delivery cost and total
It is required by WhatsApp Business
It replaces the need for records

lessons.title: How to Write High-Converting Product Descriptions
objectives: Structure a description for someone scanning rather than reading
Remove the doubts that stop a purchase
Improve a description from evidence instead of taste
lessons.notes:
Module 3 covered writing one good description. This lesson is about making descriptions convert across a whole catalogue, which is a different problem.

STRUCTURE FOR SCANNING. Nobody reads a product description as prose. One line saying exactly what it is; three or four short lines on what matters most; then the specifications as a list — size, weight, material, what is in the box; then delivery and returns. A buyer should be able to find any single fact in two seconds.

ANSWER THE DOUBT, NOT JUST THE FEATURE. Every product has one thing that stops people buying: will it fit, is it genuine, will it survive, is this the real size. Find that doubt — it is sitting in your own message history — and answer it in the description. One sentence resolving it converts better than a paragraph of adjectives.

WRITE THE MEASUREMENTS. Not 'large', but the number. 'Large' means nothing and produces returns, which cost you twice.

USE THE WORDS BUYERS USE, including how they search — brand, model, colour, size in the title and first line. This is both what a buyer scans for and what search matches.

IMPROVE FROM EVIDENCE. The questions people keep asking are the holes in your description. Every time you answer the same question twice, put the answer in the listing. Do that for a month and the listings stop generating questions and start generating orders.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — three things that belong in almost every listing here and are usually missing. DELIVERY COST AND TIME to the buyer's likely area, because it is the most common question and the most common reason a conversation stops. THE PAYMENT METHODS accepted, stated plainly, including whether pay on delivery is available. And WHAT MAKES IT GENUINE where that matters — where it was sourced, the warranty, what you do if it fails — because counterfeits are a real and reasonable worry for buyers of electronics, cosmetics and branded goods, and being specific about it is a genuine advantage over sellers who say nothing.
lessons.practice: Take five real listings and rewrite each to the structure: what it is, what matters, specifications with real measurements, delivery and returns. Then read your last fifty customer messages and list every question asked more than twice - put each answer into the relevant listing. Note which questions stop arriving afterwards.

quiz.question: How should a product description be structured?
options: For scanning - what it is, what matters, specifications, delivery and returns
As flowing prose that builds interest
With the price at the very end

quiz.question: Where do you find the doubt that stops people buying?
options: In your own message history - the questions buyers keep asking

lessons.title: How to Upsell and Cross-Sell Products on Your Online Store
objectives: Increase the value of an order without irritating the buyer
Offer the right additional item at the right moment
Use repeat purchase as the cheapest growth available
lessons.notes:
Getting a new customer is expensive. Selling more to someone already buying is nearly free, which is why this is the highest-return work in the whole course.

CROSS-SELL is the item that goes with it: the case with the phone, the charger with the device, the belt with the trousers. It works when the suggestion is genuinely useful and obviously related.

UPSELL is the better version: more capacity, longer warranty, the larger pack. It works when the difference is explained in a sentence and the price gap is small enough to feel sensible.

TIMING DECIDES WHETHER IT WORKS. Suggest the addition when the buyer has already decided on the main thing — at the point of confirming an order, not while they are still choosing. Interrupting a decision with another decision loses both.

BUNDLE where items genuinely belong together, with the bundle priced clearly below buying separately. This is the easiest version and works well on WhatsApp: 'the set, delivered, for X'.

DO NOT PUSH. Suggest once. A seller who piles on a third and fourth suggestion feels like a hawker, and the buyer starts reconsidering the whole purchase. One relevant offer, accepted or not, then complete the order cheerfully.

THE LARGEST OPPORTUNITY IS THE SECOND ORDER, and almost every small seller ignores it. Someone who bought once and was satisfied is the likeliest person to buy again. Message them when relevant stock arrives, at the point they would be running out, or with a small thank-you offer. Keeping a simple list of past customers and what they bought is the cheapest growth available to you, and it needs no advertising budget at all.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO — the natural version here is conversational, not a pop-up. On WhatsApp the seller simply says, when confirming, 'I also have the case that fits this, KSh X if you want it in the same delivery.' That works because it is true, relevant and saves a second delivery charge. And note that the strongest cross-sell argument in this market is DELIVERY ITSELF: adding to an existing order avoids paying delivery twice, which is real money and persuades far better than a discount.
lessons.practice: List your products and pair each with one genuinely useful addition and one better version. Write the one-sentence offer for each, using the shared-delivery argument where it applies. Then build a list of past customers and what they bought, and message five of them with something genuinely relevant - count how many order again.

quiz.question: When should an additional item be suggested?
options: Once the buyer has decided on the main thing, at the point of confirming
While they are still choosing the main item

quiz.question: What is the strongest cross-sell argument in this market?
options: Adding to an existing order avoids paying delivery twice
